description:
Recorded 2026-08-12 as part of op-62vf so the Edwards/Marviken agent is not blocked by surprise.

TwoFluidBoundary currently has exactly three variants, all VELOCITY boundaries: Closed, PrescribedVelocity(u), ChokedOutlet{area_fraction, ambient_pressure}. A velocity face carries no pressure sensitivity, so it stays out of the pressure matrix entirely (d_k = 0) and the pressure floats on the compliance diagonal. That is right for a closed-vessel blowdown and wrong for a pipe fed from a plenum.

drift_flux::AxialBoundary already has the two missing variants and they have no counterpart here:
  - ReservoirInlet{stagnation_pressure, stagnation_enthalpy}
  - PressureOutlet{pressure}

WHAT ADDING THEM INVOLVES in the six-equation solver, which is more than in drift flux:
  1. A half-cell pressure coefficient d = dt/(rho_face * dx/2) per PHASE at the boundary face, obtained from the 2x2 PhaseCouplingBlock rather than from a single mixture density.
  2. A Dirichlet term area * m_k_face * d_k * p_boundary on the first/last cell's pressure RHS, weighted by 1/rho_k like every other flux term in that equation.
  3. A per-phase inflow donor state: the entering fluid needs alpha_g, rho_g, rho_l, h_g and h_l, not just a mixture (p, h). A stagnation (p0, h0) does not determine a six-equation inflow state; the boundary has to say what the phase split of the incoming fluid is, or assume equilibrium and document it.

Point 3 is the real design question and it should be decided deliberately, not defaulted.

Also missing and worth deciding at the same time: the ChokedOutlet imposes the SAME velocity on both phases (no slip at the break) and hands the HEM dispatcher a mass-weighted mixture enthalpy. Both are documented at the variant, both are modelling inconsistencies, and a Marviken case may care about the first.
title: tampines TwoFluid1d: no Dirichlet-pressure boundary (ReservoirInlet / PressureOutlet) -- needed before a Marviken-style vessel discharge

description:
A TRISO 'verification' test passes while the model DISAGREES with the reference it names. Re-verified 2026-08-12; the earlier citation was wrong and the defect is DUPLICATED.

CORRECTED CITATIONS. File 1: crates/boon-lay/src/lagrangian_decay_simulator/lagrangian_diffusion/single_particle_simulator/release_fraction_crp_6_case_1a_1b.rs
  - :50 is a println!, NOT the defect (the old citation pointed here)
  - :56  let _ = catch_unwind(|| { ... })  <- the discarded assertion
  - :64  approx::assert_relative_eq!(fractional_release, 0.53, max_relative = 0.01)

File 2, NOT previously recorded, same defect verbatim:
  release_fraction_analytical_solution.rs, catch_unwind at :192,
  assert_relative_eq! against 0.53 at :200.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN 'A WEAK TEST'. The discarded assertion checks the published range 0.453 <= f <= 0.498. The assertion that SURVIVES pins f to 0.53. **0.53 lies outside 0.453-0.498.** So the test does not merely fail to check the reference -- it asserts a value that VIOLATES the reference, while silently swallowing the check that would have caught it. Both files carry the comment 'Expected range: 0.453 to 0.498' directly above the swallowed assertion, so the intent was recorded and then defeated.

The 1600 degC companion test is clean.

WHAT THIS MEANS: the CRP-6 case 1a/1b release fraction is UNVALIDATED. Nothing in the suite currently compares this model against its published reference, and the green test actively suggests otherwise. Treat any release fraction from this path as unverified until fixed.

FIX SHAPE (not applied): delete the catch_unwind and let the range assertion run. If it then fails, that is the real, useful result -- the model disagrees with CRP-6 by roughly 6-17% and that discrepancy needs investigating or documenting, not hiding. Do NOT simply widen 0.53's tolerance to make both pass; that would encode the disagreement as expected.

Found during the htr10.md re-audit (2026-08-12), which flagged that the bead's own line citation had rotted.
title: boon-lay DEFECT: TRISO release verification test asserts against itself, not the reference
